video_title: Are the Cavs the NBA's Biggest WHAT-IF? Channing & Rich Go AT IT

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye and Kendrick Perkins debate the Donovan Mitchell and Evan Mobley pairing
quotes.excerpt: I feel like that pairing does not work. You could say it does, but it does not.

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: I feel like that pairing does not work. I feel like it does not work. You could say it does, but it does not. Every year, there is too much outside noise that I see for Donovan Mitchell and Evan Mobley of who should have the ball more, who should do this, who should do that. Anytime you have a dynamic roller or versatile big like Evan Mobley, there is no way in hell that it should not work. It took a while for us to see that Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns were a match made in heaven. They found a way to make it work.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: It can work. I think those two just do not want to make it work. Anytime you have a dynamic roller or versatile big like Evan Mobley, there is no way in hell that it should not work.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye argues Donovan Mitchell is not a true number one option
quotes.excerpt: Brunson is a true number one. I don't think Donovan Mitchell is a true number one.
quotes.quote: You know the difference between Jalen Brunson and Donovan Mitchell is Brunson is a true number one. I do not think Donovan Mitchell is a true number one take you to the NBA Finals person. Do I think he is a great player? Yes. I think he is a two also. You have to bring a one in there, a real one.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye and Richard Jefferson discuss the Cavaliers' disappointing playoff performance
quotes.excerpt: There is no team that we have talked about that has bigger what-ifs than the Cavs.

text_blocks.speaker: Channing Frye
text_blocks.text: There is no team that we have talked about that has bigger what-ifs than the Cavs. The Cavs have the most pressure going into the thing. At a certain point, we have to just say, listen, if you are going to pay all that money for something, it is like going to an M. Night Shyamalan movie. You are like, oh, this is going to be great, finally. And then you are like, oh, here we go again, they got me. They got me. Thanks for believing.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: I agree. I just think that every time we do that, it gets to a space of, at the end of every season, we should trade everybody. At the end of the season when everyone loses, we should trade everybody. There is truly only six number ones out there.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson explains why it is difficult to find a true number one option
quotes.excerpt: There is only six or seven number ones out there. A lot of those guys are getting past their prime.
quotes.quote: There is truly only six number ones out there. There is Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, there is Kevin Durant, there is Stephen Curry, there is LeBron James, you can put Jayson Tatum or Jaylen Brown in that space, Nikola Jokic, Giannis Antetokounmpo, or Kawhi Leonard. Now, a lot of those guys are getting past their prime. They are getting past their prime, so it makes it more difficult. In the last six years, the number shrinks. So who do we think is a true number one that has proven it? To trade, you are basically a number two potential number one if you can prove that you can do it.
